note: Curated registry. Every attribution names who made it. 'Latest documented activity' is updated when a report is approved through the review queue.

ops.name: Storm-1516
ops.attributed: German intelligence services link it to the GRU (reported September 2026). Designation by Microsoft Threat Analysis Center.
ops.method: Fabricated videos and fake whistleblowers laundered through inauthentic news sites and paid or unwitting amplifiers, often built around sex, crime or electoral fraud.
ops.targets: Germany, France, the United States, Ukraine's European backers

latest.what: Fake video purporting to show postal ballots for the AfD being invalidated, ahead of the Saxony-Anhalt state election; attributed by German authorities.

ops.name: Doppelganger
ops.attributed: Run by the Social Design Agency and Structura, per EU sanctions designations; US Department of Justice seized dozens of its domains in September 2024.
ops.method: Clones of real news sites (Bild, The Guardian, Le Monde and others) carrying fabricated articles, pushed by bot networks.
ops.targets: Germany, France, Ukraine, the United States

latest.what: US Department of Justice domain seizures; activity documented since by multiple researchers.

ops.sanctions: Social Design Agency and Structura sanctioned by the EU

ops.name: Matryoshka
ops.attributed: Documented by VIGINUM (France) and by the researcher collective @Antibot4Navalny; Microsoft designation Storm-1679. Graphika attributed a 2026 US midterm campaign to it.
ops.method: AI-generated videos impersonating outlets such as the BBC and CNN, and mass emailing of fabricated material to newsrooms and fact-checkers to exhaust verification capacity.
ops.targets: France, Germany, Moldova, the United States

latest.what: US intelligence assessment, reported by The New York Times, of a Kremlin-authorised campaign against the midterms using AI celebrity deepfakes with fake CNN, BBC and New York Times branding.
latest.src: The New York Times, via Graphika attribution

ops.name: Pravda network
ops.attributed: Identified by VIGINUM in February 2024 and linked to the Crimea-based company TigerWeb; confirmed by DFRLab and CheckFirst.
ops.method: Roughly 90 automated sites republishing Russian state media and Telegram content at very high volume in dozens of languages, which also seeds content that AI chatbots can absorb.
ops.targets: Almost every EU member state, plus Africa and Asia

latest.what: Assessed as still active infrastructure as of 2026; TigerWeb still identified as its operator in the EU sanctions instrument as of July 2026.
latest.src: Ukraine Center for Countering Disinformation, August 2026

ops.sanctions: TigerWeb and its founder sanctioned by the EU since 15 July 2025

ops.name: CopyCop
ops.attributed: Documented by Recorded Future's Insikt Group in 2024, linked to former US deputy sheriff John Mark Dougan, who lives in Moscow.
ops.method: AI-rewritten news articles on large networks of fake local-news sites.

latest.what: Initial public exposure; activity since reported as overlapping with Storm-1516.

ops.name: Rybar
ops.attributed: Russian military-blogging network; Microsoft Threat Analysis Center designation Storm-1841.
ops.method: Telegram and X channels combining battlefield commentary with inflammatory content aimed at foreign audiences.

latest.what: Microsoft reported accounts targeting the US election with inflammatory immigration content.
